newsitem.title: CANADA: ATCO CEO says in no hurry for unit IPO.
newsitem.headline: ATCO CEO says in no hurry for unit IPO.

text.p: Utility and workforce housing conglomerate ATCO Ltd is in no hurry to float a public offering of its non-regulated businesses, ATCO Chief Executive Ron Southern said on Wednesday.

Southern told reporters after the company's annual meeting that the assets and cash flow from its Frontec construction management and logistics business and ATCO Noise Management units would make an attractive sale.
But the company was using excess cash to buy back shares under a normal course issuer bid and had no current need for new capital, he said.
The company said when it restructured its business two years ago that an initial public offering could be in the cards.
ATCO earlier today reported first-quarter earnings of C$31.5 million or C$1.03 a share on revenue of C$667.1 million.

First-quarter net earnings were down from year earlier C$39 million or C$1.28 a share in 1996, when the company posted gains of C$6.8 million on the sale of ATCOR Resources and C$2.6 million due to weather 11.3 percent colder than this year.

ATCO President and Chief Operating Officer Craighton Twa said company unit ATCO Gas Pipelines and partner Shell Canada Ltd were intent on building their proposed Alberta Pipeline Project, which would compete with NOVA Corp on its now exclusive Alberta turf.
Twa said his firm did not enter the 1.2 billion cubic feet a day project so it could be a "stalking horse" aimed at wresting cheaper tolls for producers on the NOVA Gas Transmission system.
"There seems to be a need for a project like that," he said.
He said also that company subsidiary CU Power International was evaluating several potential new cogeneration projects to build in such locations as Australia, the United Kingdom and North America.
He declined to disclose specific projects, but said none would be as big as its 1,000-megawatt Barking Station in east London.

Southern, 66, who remained chairman and CEO of ATCO after the retirements last year of former president and chief operating officer John Wood and former chief financial offer Cam Richardson, said he expected to hold the posts for at least another two years with daughter Nancy Southern holding the position of deputy chairman.
His status had been a subject of speculation as the company marked its 50th year in business.
